record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: What is the minimal k such that one can avoid abelian squares of period at least k over three letters (2 < k < 6)?

evidence.quote: What is the minimal k such that one can avoid abelian squares of period at least k over three letters (2 < k < 6)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_3 = \{0,1,2\}$ be a three-letter alphabet. A finite word $w \in \Sigma_3^*$ is called an abelian square if $w = uv$ where $|u| = |v|$ and $v$ is a permutation of the letters of $u$ (i.e., $u$ and $v$ have the same Parikh vector). The integer $|u|$ is called the period of the abelian square $uv$. An infinite word $\mathbf{w} \in \Sigma_3^{\mathbb{N}}$ is said to avoid abelian squares of period at least $k$ if no factor of $\mathbf{w}$ is an abelian square $uv$ with $|u| \geq k$.

It is known that there is no infinite word over $\Sigma_3$ that avoids all abelian squares (i.e., the case $k=1$ is impossible), while for sufficiently large $k$ such infinite words exist (in particular, for $k \geq 6$). 

Determine the minimal integer $k$ with $2 < k < 6$ (that is, $k \in \{3,4,5\}$) such that there exists an infinite word over the three-letter alphabet $\Sigma_3$ avoiding every abelian square of period at least $k$.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal active research on avoiding long abelian repetitions over small alphabets (e.g., Rao–Rosenfeld, "Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions," Math. Comp. 2016, and Rosenfeld's PhD thesis), with related Mäkelä-style conjectures and computer-experimental partial results. However, no source explicitly identifies the exact minimal $k \in \{3,4,5\}$ for which abelian squares of period at least $k$ can be avoided over three letters. The status appears unresolved in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions
status_evidence.snippet: One can avoid 2-abelian-squares of period at least 2 in infinite ternary words... Mäkelä asked whether you can avoid abelian-squares of the form uv where |u| ≥ 2 over three letters.
status_evidence.claim: Related avoidability problems on long abelian repetitions over ternary alphabets are studied with partial computer-aided answers, but the exact minimal threshold k for ordinary abelian squares is not pinned down.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of Abelian Repetitions in Words (Rosenfeld thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses avoidance of abelian and k-abelian powers over binary and ternary alphabets.
status_evidence.claim: The thesis surveys avoidance of long abelian squares over ternary alphabets without resolving the precise minimal period threshold in the range considered.
